then.say: Another one up from the road. Sit, if your legs allow it. This is Wick's Rest, the last honest shrine this side of the Abbey.
Rest at it and your wounds close and your phial fills. The dead get up again too, I'm afraid. Nothing is free.
Warm. The Drip hasn't touched you at all. Hm.

else.say: Still warm? Good. Keep it that way.

menu.text: I want to grow stronger. (Level up)

then.say: Stronger. Everyone asks for that, sooner or later. There's a way. It isn't a kind one.
The Tallow you carry was people once. Hold it to the flame and it gives back a little of what they had: breath, grip, blood.
I'll do it. Someone should be watching when it's done.

else.say: Hold it to the flame, then.

menu.text: Can you undo what I've become? (Reset stats)

do.say: I can take it back out of you. All of it: every point, back to what you were on the road. The Tallow comes back too.

menu.text: Do it. (Reset every stat; get all the Tallow back)

do.say: Hold still. This is the part that stings.
As you like.
The slow death. First cold fingers, then a shine on the skin, then you're a candle that walks. The Great Wick keeps it back.
Kept it back.
The Guttering Abbey, up the Hill Stair. Penitents go there to give themselves to the flame. None come back down.
The Tollwarden keeps its gatehouse. He takes a toll from everyone who passes. What he takes, you'll see.
Dead? ...
You tell her his last words: that Anselm kept the count.
Anselm. I haven't heard that name said aloud in twenty years.
He wasn't cruel, you know. He was the only one up there who looked at their faces. Somebody had to.
Go on, then. You have his key. Go and see what he counted.
She reads the first page. Then the second. Her hands stop shaking somewhere around the tenth.
Names and weights. He wrote down the weights.
I knew. Not this. But I knew enough, and I kept the shrine lit and I didn't ask, because the shrine was all these people had.
Keep it. Somebody has to carry it up to him, and it can't be me. Not yet.

then.say: Dead. Then... no. Wait. You're carrying something with a knot I know.
Give me my sister's letter first. Whatever you decide about me after, let me have read it.
You hand her the Chandler's Ledger. She reads the first page, then the second. Her hands stop shaking somewhere around the tenth.
Names and weights. He wrote down the weights.

else.say: Dead. Then it's over. Up there, anyway.
I owe you all of it, so here it is. Then you can say what I am.
Twenty years ago the Order came down to this shrine with a cart and a ledger. The Great Wick wanted feeding, they said, and a Sister who kept quiet could keep her flame.
So I sent them up. The tired ones. The sick ones. The ones nobody would come looking for. I told them the Abbey would take them in, and it did.
Every point of breath and grip I gave you came out of what they boiled down. I held it to the flame and told myself I was giving it back.
She takes the snuffer from its hook on the shrine and puts it in your hand.
You're the only one who's gone all the way up and come back down warm. So it's yours to say.

menu.text: I forgive you. (She stays; Wick's Rest stays lit)

do.say: You hang the snuffer back on its hook.
Then I'll keep the flame. Not for them up there. For whoever comes up the road next, and I'll look at their faces, the way Anselm did.
Here. I kept this back for myself, for the day the Drip came for me. I don't think I'm afraid of it any more.

menu.text: I condemn you. (She leaves; her Wick goes cold)

do.say: You say it. She nods, as if she'd written the words herself.
Yes. That's fair. That's the first fair thing anyone has said in this yard for twenty years.
I'll walk the road down. Somebody should carry the names away from here and say them where it's quiet.
This Wick won't answer anyone once I'm gone. Hold your Tallow to any other flame. It'll listen without me.
And take what's in the box under my bench. It was never mine.
She took nothing but her shawl. Behind you, the Wick of Wick's Rest gutters, and goes out.

toast: Wick's Rest can no longer be rested at or travelled to. Level up at any other Wick from its menu.

do.say: She takes the snuffer back.
Take your time. I've had twenty years of it.
Lighter. I didn't know a person could be lighter at my age.
Whatever's drinking the Wick up there, it hasn't finished. When you go up the lift, I'll be here. Somebody should be.

menu.text: What is behind the locked gate?

do.say: The carters' road, down to the Tallow Works. The carts go through full and come back empty. The Tollwarden has the key.
The orchard valley, past the collapsed gate on the road. I was born there. That was a long time ago and a different woman.
The Synod has been busy there, I hear. If you go, mind the bees. They were never gentle, even when things were good.

menu.text: I bring a letter from Bloomhollow.

do.say: She sees the pressed blossom under the twine before she sees anything else, and sits down.
Hild. That's Hild's knot. She could never tie a proper one.
She reads it once, quickly, and then again very slowly.
She's still there. In the orchard, with the Synod at the gate and the Skep gone wrong. Of course she is. She's more stubborn than I ever was devout.
Twenty years I've let her write into silence. I told myself a Sister of the Wick has no family but the flame.
She takes something small from a fold of her habit, wraps it in a page, and seals the page with grey wax from the shrine.
Take her this. Don't read it. And don't let her come up here after me. Promise me that.
I don't know. And I'd rather not guess out loud. Keep your gloves on around the Order.
The flame keep you.
